scenes.storyState: The party is gathering information in Hamack; if the job branch is active, Sion and Karu can help with inventory.
scenes.purpose: Translate the complete early inventory-job offer, refusal, acceptance, and later job-ending dialogue.
previousContext: The party has arrived in Hamack and can speak to a young woman offering inventory work.
followingContext: The accept branch reaches a short shop-clerk sequence; other job records are later conditional interactions.
branchAlternatives: 052000:072 is the offer; 057 responds to declining, while 051000:027 resolves acceptance. 073 is a conditional alternative line. 051000:022 and 023 are distinct conditional job outcomes, not adjacent stages.
evidence: Fresh replay decoded text and RE-confirmed job branch closure.
uncertainty: The employer/shop identity is not named in the cited dialogue.
notes: Control-only dispatcher 052000:058 is not given a canonical line.
scenes.reviewNote: Re-read the whole offer, acceptance, refusal, repeat and dismissal alternatives against source after the 2026-09-24 playtest. The woman sorts stock as a part-time job and asks for help; preserve the distinction between no-pay dismissal and the 200-credit outcome.

records.canonicalEnglish: Young Woman: I have a part-time job sorting stock, but it’s a lot to handle alone... Say, could you give me a hand?

context.speaker: Young Woman
context.intent: Offers the party part-time work organizing inventory.
uncertainty: The task is inventory organization; no employer or exact pay terms are stated here.
notes: Connected to the conditional inventory-work branch in Hamack.

records.canonicalEnglish: Young Woman: I may look busy, but sometimes I’m actually free.

context.speaker: Young Woman
context.intent: Ambient alternate line when her job offer is unavailable.
uncertainty: This is an alternative response, not a continuation of the job offer.
notes: Connected to the conditional inventory-work branch in Hamack.

records.canonicalEnglish: Young Woman: Aw, darn! I was going to pay you generously for the part-time work.

context.speaker: Young Woman
context.intent: Responds to a refusal by lamenting that she meant to offer generous part-time wages.
uncertainty: No precise wage or work schedule is stated.
notes: Connected to the conditional inventory-work branch in Hamack.

records.canonicalEnglish:
Sion: OK! Leave it to me!
Shoko: Honestly, Sion is weak around girls. Karu, what will you do?
Karu: I’ll work with Sion.
Shoko: All right, I suppose I’ll wait at the hotel. Make sure you earn plenty!
Narration: And so, Sion became a shop clerk.

context.speaker: Mixed party / narration
context.intent: Resolves acceptance of the inventory job: Karu volunteers, Shoko waits at the hotel, and Sion/Karu work as clerks.
uncertainty: The source identifies the pair as shop clerks; it does not name the employer or shop.
notes: Connected to the conditional inventory-work branch in Hamack.

records.canonicalEnglish:
Shop Woman: I’m sorry, but I only need people who can work seriously.
Shop Woman: I’m afraid I have to let you go.
Shop Woman: I can’t pay you any wages, either.

context.speaker: Shop Woman
context.intent: A later conditional job interaction dismisses the worker and says no wages can be paid.
uncertainty: The source says she cannot pay wages; it does not specify a raise or explain why the worker is unsuitable.
notes: Connected to the conditional inventory-work branch in Hamack.

records.canonicalEnglish:
Shop Woman: Good work.
Shop Woman: This is sudden, but we’re fully staffed now, so we don’t need you anymore.
Shop Woman: I’ve added a little extra to your pay, so please accept it.
Narration: You received 200 credits.

context.speaker: Shop Woman / narration
context.intent: Ends a job after staffing needs change and awards 200 credits.
uncertainty: The source says staffing is now sufficient; it gives no duration of employment or breakdown of the bonus.
notes: Connected to the conditional inventory-work branch in Hamack.
